headings: 5.5 WORK DONE BY A VARIABLE FORCE
pages.page_summary: The page discusses kinetic energy and work done by a variable force. It includes a table of typical kinetic energies for various objects (car, athlete, bullet, stone, rain drop, air molecule). It presents Example 5.4, a ballistics problem calculating the emergent speed of a bullet after passing through plywood. It then introduces the concept of work done by a variable force, explaining it as the area under a force-displacement curve, and derives the definite integral form of work.
knowledge_points: Kinetic energy is the capacity of an object to do work by virtue of its motion.
Table 5.2 lists typical kinetic energies for various objects.
Example 5.4 calculates the emergent speed of a bullet (mass 50.0 g, initial speed 200 m/s) after losing 90% of its kinetic energy, resulting in a final speed of 63.2 m/s.
Work done by a variable force is the area under the force-displacement curve.
The work done by a variable force can be expressed as a definite integral of force over displacement: W = ∫ F(x) dx.
